title: Crash in nvd3dum on DDrawCompat's worker thread when a D3D7 game releases its textures (stale 3840x2160 surface memory)

events.body_markdown:
**Game:** Interstate '82 (GOG, DirectDraw 7 / Direct3D 7), with a resolution patch to run at 3840x2160.
**DDrawCompat:** v0.7.1, and also the test build from #424 (v0.7.1-dirty). `FullscreenMode = borderless`, `DisplayAspectRatio = app`, `CompatFixes = singlemonitor`.
**System:** Windows 11 25H2 (26200), RTX 4070 Ti, driver 32.0.15.9579, desktop 3840x2160 @ 120 Hz.

### Symptom

Crash to desktop when leaving a mission ("Exit Mission"). Not every time — today it was 2 crashes in about 25 mission exits, and 11 crashes in total since 2026-09-19. Every one has the same signature:

```
Exception:  0xC0000005, nvd3dum.dll 32.0.15.9579 + 0x014EA564
nvd3dum!SetDependencyInfo+0xb10c4:
    movdqa xmm0, xmmword ptr [esi]      ; esi = 03d3ec00 -> MEM_FREE
```

### The two threads at the time of the crash

The faulting thread is DDrawCompat's worker thread:

```
00 nvd3dum!SetDependencyInfo+0xb10c4
01 nvd3dum+0x137412c
02 nvd3dum+0x136b444
03 nvd3dum+0x136b551
04 nvd3dum+0x13fd93d
05 nvd3dum!QueryOglResource+0x18be7
06 ddraw+0xb1a78            (test build; v0.7.1 offsets differ slightly)
07 ddraw+0xb4176
08 ddraw+0x14d3cc
09 ddraw+0x14ce2b
0a ddraw+0x14e088
0b ddraw!WinWatchOpen+0x80718
0c kernel32!BaseThreadInitThunk+0x19
```

At the same moment the game's main thread is tearing the mission down and releasing a texture, blocked on the DirectDraw lock:

```
00 ntdll!NtWaitForAlertByThreadId+0xc
...
04 ntdll!RtlEnterCriticalSection+0x63
05 ddraw (system)!AcquireDDThreadLock+0x16
06 d3dim!DIRECT3DTEXTUREI::Release+0x12
07 i82sim!...                (game code: mission teardown)
```

In some of the older minidumps the main thread waits on a critical section inside DDrawCompat instead (`ddraw+0xb555a`, v0.7.1). The worker thread looks the same in all of them.

### What the full dump shows

I have a full-memory dump of today's crash (1 GB). These are the parts that seem relevant:

- The source pointer `03d3ec00` is in a **freed** region (`03d31000-03d40000`, `MEM_FREE`). The destination (`edi`) is a 3 MB `PAGE_READWRITE | PAGE_WRITECOMBINE` region, so this looks like a copy from system memory into an upload buffer.
- `edx = 0x3c00` (15360 = 3840 × 4).
- **The same address, `03d3ec00`, appears in 6 of the 7 dumps**, across game sessions on different days. The seventh, from 2026-09-20, has a different address and `edx = 0x640`.
- Several heap objects still point at `03d3ec00`. One looks like a DirectDraw surface global:

  ```
  07462ea8  0071bfe0 03d3ec00 00007800 0f000870     ; fpVidMem = 03d3ec00, pitch 0x7800, 2160 x 3840
  07462eb8  00000000 00000000 00000020 00000040     ; DDPIXELFORMAT: size 32, DDPF_RGB
  07462ec8  00000000 00000020 00ff0000 0000ff00     ; 32 bpp, X8R8G8B8 masks
  ```

  Another looks like the surface info passed to the driver when the resource was created:

  ```
  1407fdb8  00000f00 00000870 00000000 03d3ec00 00007800     ; 3840, 2160, 0, pSysMem, pitch
  ```

So a 3840x2160 X8R8G8B8 system-memory surface still exists as a DirectDraw object and as a driver resource, but its memory has already been freed. The worker thread then hands it to the driver as a copy source. I can't tell from the dump which surface this is or who freed it. Its size matches the desktop and the game resolution, and it appears while the game is releasing textures on mission exit. That is as far as I can take it.

The full dump is available if it would help. It is 1 GB, so I'd share it by link rather than attach it here.

Possibly related: #614, where I reported a divide-by-zero on the same worker thread.

I have minidumps of this crash from the official v0.7.1 as well, so here are the stacks with symbols. The faulting thread is the same in all three I looked at:

```
nvd3dum!SetDependencyInfo+0xb10c4
...
nvd3dum!QueryOglResource+0x18be7
ddraw!D3dDdi::Resource::copySubResourceRegion+0x118          D3dDdi\Resource.cpp @ 525
ddraw!D3dDdi::Resource::presentationBlt+0x266                D3dDdi\Resource.cpp @ 1339
ddraw!`anonymous namespace'::presentationBlt+0x17c           DDraw\RealPrimarySurface.cpp @ 187
ddraw!`anonymous namespace'::present+0x35b                   DDraw\RealPrimarySurface.cpp @ 288
ddraw!`anonymous namespace'::updateThreadProc+0x238          DDraw\RealPrimarySurface.cpp @ 466
```

Line 1339 is the `D3DDDIPOOL_SYSTEMMEM` branch, which copies the presentation source into a temp texture. That matches the full dump: the source is a 3840x2160 system-memory surface whose memory is already freed.

The main thread differs between dumps, but it is always blocked somewhere during mission teardown:

- in `d3dim!DIRECT3DTEXTUREI::Release`, on `AcquireDDThreadLock`, while the game releases its textures (one v0.7.1 dump, and the full dump from the test build);
- in `Gdi::Window::updateWindowPos` (`Gdi\Window.cpp @ 795`), on DDrawCompat's `D3dDdi::ScopedCriticalSection`;
- in `defPaintProc` (`Gdi\User32WndProcs.cpp @ 157`), on the same critical section.

So it looks like the update thread presents from the game's system-memory primary, or its back buffer, after the game has started tearing it down.

I've switched to your build with symbols from #614. If this crash happens again with it, I can send a full dump that you can symbolize.

It happened again, on leaving a mission, this time with your build from #614 (the one with symbols, `ddraw.dll` sha256 `bab42ec7…`). So that build doesn't fix this one, which is expected, since it's a different issue. The full dump has symbols now, so here is what it shows.

Same path as before, and again the same source address:

```
nvd3dum!SetDependencyInfo+0xb10c4                             movdqa xmm0,[esi]   esi = 03d3ec00 (MEM_FREE)
...
ddraw!D3dDdi::Resource::copySubResourceRegion+0x118          D3dDdi\Resource.cpp @ 525
ddraw!D3dDdi::Resource::presentationBlt+0x266                D3dDdi\Resource.cpp @ 1339
ddraw!`anonymous namespace'::presentationBlt+0x17c           DDraw\RealPrimarySurface.cpp @ 187
ddraw!`anonymous namespace'::present+0x362                   DDraw\RealPrimarySurface.cpp @ 288
ddraw!`anonymous namespace'::updateThreadProc+0x238          DDraw\RealPrimarySurface.cpp @ 466
```

In `D3dDdi::Resource::presentationBlt`, `origSrcResource` is:

```
m_fixedData.Format   D3DDDIFMT_X8R8G8B8
m_fixedData.Pool     D3DDDIPOOL_SYSTEMMEM
pSurfList[0]         Width 0xf00, Height 0x870, pSysMem 0x03d3ec00, SysMemPitch 0x7800
m_lockResource       empty
```

`src` in `present()` / `presentationBlt()` is `0x0ec44458`.

**At the same moment, both `g_primarySurface` (PrimarySurface.cpp) and `g_frontBuffer` (RealPrimarySurface.cpp) are already null.** So the primary appears to have been released, while the update thread is still presenting from a surface that looks like the former primary: same size and format, system memory, and freed memory behind it. No other thread is inside a surface release at that point. The game's main thread is waiting on `AcquireDDThreadLock` in `d3dim!DIRECT3DTEXTUREI::Release`, and the update thread holds that lock from `updateThreadProc` line 465. I couldn't work out from the dump how `src` can still be non-null in the same `flush()` in which `getPrimary()` would now return null. That part is for you.

I can share the full dump (about 1.1 GB, taken with your build and its PDB) by link if you want it.

I have the game on GOG so I'll try to reproduce it myself, as that would make debugging much easier, especially since debug logs would be useful in addition to the crash dump in this case. But hold on to that dump in case I can't reproduce it.

Which resolution patch were you referring to? It might be important for the repro, though I don't think so at the moment.

It's my own: [interstate82-win11-compat-shim](https://github.com/SputnikKaputtnik/interstate82-win11-compat-shim) (release v1.2). It's a `dinput.dll` proxy that widens the game's display-mode filter so that 1920x1080 and 3840x2160 are offered in place of 1280x1024 and 1024x768. It also works around a mission-load crash in `i82sim.dll` and fixes key names for in-game binding. The release includes the DDrawCompat profile I use (`DDrawCompat-i82stubz.ini`: borderless, and `SupportedResolutions` with the two added modes).

I don't think the crash depends on it, though. It already happened before the resolution part existed, at the game's own 4:3 modes, and one of the v0.7.1 dumps has a source pitch of `0x640` instead of `0x3c00`, so a smaller surface. All the recent ones were at 3840x2160.

I'll keep the dump.

Thanks, I found it already in the meantime. I actually need your patch anyway, otherwise starting a mission reliably crashes.

But now I have another problem: once I start a mission (I chose "instant action"), the keyboard stops working and only responds to DDrawCompat's own hotkeys. I can't drive the car or exit the mission. The keyboard still seems to work in the menu, or at least I can assign new keys in the Controls menu. Do you know what could be the issue here?

Thanks for trying it! I haven't seen that exact behaviour with the shim, but it's close to what happened before I had it: on Windows 11 DirectInput returned empty key names for the keyboard, the game couldn't register its in-mission controls, and the menus still worked.

The quickest way to tell is `dinput_msgbox.log` next to `i82stubz.exe`. The game reports binding problems in `CInput...` message boxes, which would sit behind the fullscreen window, so the shim answers them and writes their text to that log instead. In a working setup it only contains lines like

```
[swallowed] CInputBinding::bindControl: Only button controls may assigned to BINDTYPE_PRESS
```

once per mission start. If yours has other `CInput` lines (e.g. that a control doesn't exist), that's the key-name problem, and the text will say which names it didn't recognise.

What I'd try first, since the menu still takes keys for you: in my setup, part of the fix was re-assigning **every** key by hand under Options → Controls → Key Configuration and then pressing SAVE. The game keeps the active bindings in `bindings.usr` in the game folder, which the GOG release doesn't ship. It's only written when you save in that screen. I never narrowed down which of the steps mattered most, so this is from experience, not a diagnosis.

Things I've ruled out or would check:
- A missing or 64-bit `dinput_orig.dll` doesn't cause this. I just tested it: without it the game doesn't start at all ("unable to start due to your display settings").
- Which keyboard layout / Windows display language are you using? I've only tested with German.
- Driving is on the numpad by default (Numpad 8/2/4/6), but Escape should still work, so that alone doesn't explain it.

I actually found a workaround in the meantime: I replaced dinput_orig.dll with [dinputto8](https://github.com/elishacloud/dinputto8), and that fixed the keys.

But I'm not having any luck with reproducing the crash. I was already able to exit the instant action 50 times in a row without any crashes. Could you please share your crash dump?

Thanks, and thanks for the dinputto8 hint. It pointed me in the right direction. The names DirectInput hands out depend on its language resources. Loaded from System32, it finds them and returns localized names: on my German system "Tastatur", "Maus", "Leertaste" and so on, and Interstate '82 can't register its controls with those. The renamed copy in the game folder has no language file next to it, so it returns empty names, which the game copes with. So the shim only worked by accident until now. I'm testing a version that handles the names itself and doesn't need `dinput_orig.dll` at all.

Here's the dump: https://1drv.ms/u/c/68a6b10bc923e32a/IQA-xSPCouyISK9HlJQrL1rZAR70gpN0tck2aLgPVV9u-cY?e=4iLXrU
It's `i82stubz.exe.10120.dmp`, a full-memory dump, 80 MB as 7z (1.2 GB unpacked). It was taken with your build from #614 (`ddraw.dll` sha256 `bab42ec7…`, with its PDB), at 3840x2160. The source address is `03d3ec00` again, same path as before.

On reproducing it, this might be the more useful part. That dump comes from a session where I was only trying to take three screenshots of the game's menus. It took many attempts, because the Snipping Tool overlay kept losing the foreground right away. During that session the game crashed seven times in about 70 minutes, without entering a mission.

I've now reproduced it on purpose, though not reliably. In the menu I pressed Win+Shift+S. The overlay took the foreground at 23:06:38.458, and the crash was logged at 23:06:38.647, less than 0.2 s later. It's the same crash, with your build from #614. This one is the menu variant: source `01e9f600`, pitch `0x640`, which I think is the menu's 800x600x16 primary. Overall that's 1 crash in 3 tries with Win+Shift+S and 0 in 3 with the Print key, which opens the same overlay on current Windows 11. Every time it didn't crash, the overlay lost the foreground again after about 100 ms, apparently back to the game. Still, in my case menu + Snipping Tool overlay crashes far more often than exiting missions does. I can share this dump as well.

Quick heads-up so you don't spend more time on this: I'll continue testing on my side for now. Two things turned up in the meantime:

- The display-mode error cascade I described as symptom 1 in #614 looks like it's caused by my resolution patch, not by DDrawCompat. It happens on "Restart Mission" at the two modes the patch adds (1920x1080 and 3840x2160), but not in three restarts at 800x600, which the patch doesn't touch. Please disregard it for now.
- For this crash, `AltTabFix = keepvidmem(1)` stops the variant triggered by Alt+Tab: nine Alt+Tabs in a mission without a crash, where it used to crash within three to five. The crash when leaving or restarting a mission still happens with it.

I'll report back once I know more. Thanks a lot for your help so far!

Thanks for the dump! The situation is fairly clear from it. Since the primary surface was currently in a lost state, DDrawCompat is trying to present from the shared GDI surface (VirtualScreen.cpp) until the primary is recovered. This encompasses the bounding box of your entire desktop, which is quite huge, partly due to the odd placement of your secondary monitor at coordinates (-3840, -2090). This results in a total desktop resolution of 7680x4250 (see g_bounds in VirtualScreen.cpp).

The odd part that leads to the crash is that g_surfaceView is NULL. This could only happen if reallocating it failed at line 319, possibly due to running out of virtual memory, or due to memory fragmentation. You should probably add some info log there that prints the new value of g_surfaceView and the return value of GetLastError(). I imagine you will see it become NULL right before the crash with some out of memory error returned by GetLastError().

This also explains the recurring 03d3ec00 pointer that you keep encountering. It is calculated in getSurfaceDesc at line 220, and will point to some bogus area due to g_surfaceView being NULL. If you follow the calculation there, it becomes:
0 + 0 + (0 - (-2090)) * 30720 + (0 - (-3840)) * 32 / 8 =
2090 * 30720 + 3840 * 4 =
64204800 + 15360 =
64220160 = 0x3D3EC00

In your case I think you can add GdiInterops=none to your configuration, since this game doesn't seem to require any GDI interop anyway. That would remove the need for the shared GDI surface and DDrawCompat won't try to allocate it all.
Alternatively, you could try to increase the virtual memory limit of the executable to 4GB with the Large Address Aware flag, but I haven't checked if the game is stable with that setting.

Another idea I have from DDrawCompat's point of view is that I could try to do these large allocations only once at startup, matching your full virtual desktop resolution. I think I would have to actually allocate this twice due to the fact that later I might need a g_lastFullscreenSurfaceView as well. That's about 2x124 MB upfront allocation, but it could help avoid the fragmentation issue at least, since these would never have to be reallocated (unless you later attach another monitor to your desktop, but I wouldn't recommend that while running a ddraw game anyway). The rest of the game would probably fit just fine into the default 2GB limit.

Thanks a lot, that explains everything, including the `03d3ec00` puzzle.

`GdiInterops = none` fixes it here. I automated the test so that it runs the same way every time: instant action, then Esc → "Restart Mission" in a loop, at 3840x2160.

- Before (v0.7.1 and your builds from #614/#424): 7 crashes in 39 restarts, spread over 3840x2160, 1920x1080 and 800x600. So it doesn't depend on the resolution patch.
- With `GdiInterops = none`: 16 restarts in a row in one session, no crash.

`AltTabFix = keepvidmem(1)` was set in both runs, so it's not what made the difference.

I'll add `GdiInterops = none` to the profile that ships with the patch. Doing the large allocations once at startup sounds like a good idea for - granted, weird - setups like mine. Thanks again for taking the time to dig into this!

If you have some time to do a bit of stress testing, could you please test this patch **without** GdiInterops=none?
[ddraw.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32659459/ddraw.zip) ([diff.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32659462/diff.txt) compared to v0.7.1)

This implements what I suggested earlier about keeping only a single large VirtualScreen allocation. I actually didn't need a second allocation with these changes, after all.
It also includes the patch from https://github.com/narzoul/DDrawCompat/issues/614#issuecomment-5803143242 to exclude the other crash possibilities.

Hopefully now it shouldn't crash even if GdiInterops is enabled, which could be useful for other games.

By the way, I wanted to mention that your project documentation claims that DDrawCompat only supports 4:3 resolutions by default, but this is not true. The "native" option in SupportedResolutions includes all resolutions that your display already supports, irrespective of the aspect ratio. So 1920x1080 and 3840x2160 would already be included without changing the default SupportedResolutions setting.
Those low-resolution 4:3 modes were only listed explicitly because some modern systems don't support them by default, but they are required by many old games.

Thanks, both noted.

I'll stress-test the patch without `GdiInterops = none` over the next few days, with the same automated Restart Mission loop and campaign mission starts at 3840x2160, receiver still at (-3840, -2090), so it's comparable to the 7 crashes in 39 restarts from before. I'll report back here.

And thanks for the correction on `SupportedResolutions`, I had that wrong. I'll fix the documentation.

Thanks for the build! I ran it the same way as before: Instant Action, then "Restart Mission" in a loop, at 3840x2160 on the same two-display setup, with `GdiInterops` left at its default (`all`) and `AltTabFix = keepvidmem(1)` set, as in the earlier runs.

- Your test build: 1 crash in 40 restarts.
- Before (v0.7.1 and the #614/#424 builds): 7 crashes in 39 restarts.

So it's a clear improvement, but not quite gone. The one crash was an access violation at the fourth restart of the first session. Unfortunately `CrashDump` was still off at that point, and after I turned it on (`CrashDump = full`), the remaining 36 restarts ran without a crash, so I have no dump of it. The DDrawCompat log of that session just ends without any error message.

Thanks for testing! It's a pity you didn't get a crash dump. Most likely this was a different issue than the ones you reported so far.

I have a lot of local fixes piled up now, so maybe it's something I already fixed anyway. I'll start regression testing soon and hopefully make a new public release within the next few weeks, depending on how many new regressions I find. Then you can retest with the new release, if you're still up for it.
